title: Basel III / IV
full_name: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision Capital Requirements
penalties: Capital add-ons; distribution restrictions
content: Basel III establishes global standards for bank capital adequacy, stress testing, liquidity risk management, and the data aggregation principles of BCBS 239 that underpin regulatory reporting.

title: SOX
penalties: Up to $5M and 20 years imprisonment for executives
content: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act mandates strict reforms to improve financial disclosures, requiring executives to personally certify the accuracy of financial statements and internal controls over financial reporting.

title: PCI DSS
full_name: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0
penalties: $5,000–$100,000/month; loss of card acceptance
content: PCI DSS v4.0 is the security standard for all organizations that store, process, or transmit cardholder data — with enhanced requirements for web skimming prevention, customized implementation, and continuous compliance.

title: GDPR
penalties: €20M or 4% of global annual turnover
content: The GDPR is the world's most consequential data privacy regulation, applying extraterritorially to any organization processing EU residents' personal data, with rights to erasure, portability, and algorithmic transparency.

title: GLBA
penalties: Up to $51,744 per violation per day
content: GLBA requires financial institutions to safeguard customer nonpublic personal information with a comprehensive written security program, with the 2023 Safeguards Rule update adding specific technical requirements including MFA, encryption, and continuous monitoring.

title: HIPAA
full_name: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
penalties: $100–$50,000 per violation; up to $1.9M/category/year
content: HIPAA establishes administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for protected health information, with the HITECH Act and Omnibus Rule expanding business associate liability and creating the breach notification framework.

title: HITECH
full_name: Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act
penalties: Up to $1.9M per violation category per year
content: HITECH strengthened HIPAA enforcement with tiered civil monetary penalties, extended direct liability to business associates, and established the 60-day breach notification requirement that governs healthcare data breach response.

title: CCPA / CPRA
full_name: California Consumer Privacy Act / Privacy Rights Act
audit_frequency: CPPA complaint-driven; annual cybersecurity audits for high-risk processing
penalties: $2,500–$7,500 per violation; $750 per consumer per data breach
content: CCPA/CPRA grants California consumers comprehensive rights over personal information collection, use, and sale, with the CPRA creating the California Privacy Protection Agency as an independent enforcement authority and adding new Sensitive Personal Information protections.

title: ISO 27001
penalties: Certification suspension/withdrawal
content: ISO 27001:2022 is the world's most widely adopted information security management system standard, requiring organizations to establish a risk-based ISMS with 93 controls across organizational, people, physical, and technological themes.

title: NIST CSF
penalties: None (Voluntary)
content: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework provides a risk-based approach to cybersecurity organized around six core functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, and Recover — the most widely adopted cybersecurity management framework globally.

title: SOC 2
penalties: Loss of certification; commercial consequences
content: SOC 2 Type II is the de facto security certification for cloud service providers and SaaS companies, assessing the design and operating effectiveness of controls across the Trust Services Criteria: Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy.

title: NERC CIP
full_name: North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection
audit_frequency: Periodic Regional Entity audits (typically every 3 years)
penalties: Up to $1,000,000 per violation per day
content: NERC CIP standards are mandatory enforceable requirements for bulk electric system operators, covering cybersecurity across 12 standards from categorization through supply chain risk management — with penalties that make compliance failure existential.

title: FedRAMP
full_name: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program
penalties: Revocation of authorization; removal from FedRAMP Marketplace
content: FedRAMP provides a standardized 'do once, use many' approach to cloud security authorization for federal agencies, with tiered baselines (Low/Moderate/High) and continuous monitoring requirements that enable reuse of cloud service authorizations across the federal enterprise.

title: FISMA
audit_frequency: Annual FISMA reporting; continuous monitoring; 3-year ATO cycle
penalties: Budget consequences; ATO revocation; contractor debarment
content: FISMA requires federal agencies and their contractors to implement information security programs consistent with NIST SP 800-53, operationalized through the Risk Management Framework's categorize-select-implement-assess-authorize-monitor lifecycle.

title: CMMC 2.0
penalties: Contract ineligibility; False Claims Act treble damages; debarment
content: CMMC 2.0 introduces mandatory third-party certification for DoD contractors handling Controlled Unclassified Information, building on NIST SP 800-171's 110 practices with the addition of independent C3PAO assessment requirements that took effect in 2025.

title: DORA
audit_frequency: Ongoing NCA supervision; TLPT every 3 years; annual ICT risk assessment
penalties: Up to 2% of total annual worldwide turnover; €5M for critical ICT providers
content: DORA establishes a comprehensive ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing, and third-party oversight framework for EU financial entities and their critical technology service providers — in force from January 17, 2025.

title: FERPA
full_name: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act
penalties: Loss of all federal funding (rarely exercised); corrective action
content: FERPA protects the privacy of student education records at all federally-funded educational institutions, granting parents and eligible students rights to access, correct, and control disclosure of education records — including AI-generated assessments and learning analytics data.

title: HITRUST CSF
audit_frequency: Annual (e1/i1); biennial r2 with annual interim assessment
penalties: Certification withdrawal; commercial contract consequences
content: HITRUST CSF harmonizes HIPAA, NIST, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and state regulations into a single certifiable framework — making it the de facto security certification for healthcare organizations and their business associates handling protected health information.

title: EU AI Act
audit_frequency: Pre-market conformity assessment; post-market monitoring ongoing
penalties: €35M or 7% of global turnover for prohibited AI; €15M or 3% for high-risk violations
content: The EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive AI regulation, using a risk-based classification (Prohibited / High-Risk / Limited-Risk / Minimal-Risk) to impose transparency, documentation, human oversight, and conformity assessment requirements on AI systems placed on the EU market.

title: NIST SP 800-53
audit_frequency: Continuous monitoring; formal assessments on 3-year ATO cycle
penalties: Loss of ATO; budget consequences; contractor debarment
content: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 is the comprehensive federal security and privacy control catalog with 20 control families, integrated privacy controls, and AI governance requirements — the foundational reference for FISMA, FedRAMP, and CMMC compliance programs.

title: MiFID II
full_name: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II / MiFIR
audit_frequency: Ongoing NCA supervision; annual best execution reporting
penalties: Up to €5M or 10% of annual turnover; withdrawal of authorization
content: MiFID II governs investment services across the EEA with specific requirements for transaction reporting accuracy, algorithmic trading governance, best execution documentation, and investor protection — creating direct data quality and AI governance obligations for investment firms.
